---
title: "Stage 7 — compare against what was built"
---

The stage that tells you whether any of it was right.

## What this is

Here, the study already had analysis datasets built by a programmer working from the same plan.
Comparing the executed result against them is the strongest external check available, because
the two implementations are genuinely independent.

**Most readers will not have that, and it is worth being clear about why.** An independently
built implementation exists when someone has already done the work by hand — which is true of a
study being re-examined, and false of one being specified for the first time. On a new study
there is nothing to compare against, and in the world these standards are aiming at there is
nothing to compare against *by design*: the point of a declared specification is to stop having
two implementations that must be reconciled.

So this stage is partly transitional. It is most useful now, while both worlds exist.

**What to do instead, when there is nothing to compare against.** Reproduce the engine's number
outside the engine, using the engine's own selection — the filters and joins its console
reported at stage 6. That is a weaker check than an independent implementation, because it
shares the engine's assumptions, but it is the one that actually found the mechanism described
below: not by disagreeing with the answer, but by making the engine's choices explicit enough to
see.

## What you do

Fit the same model on the study's own derived variables and compare. Where the two disagree,
reproduce the engine's number outside the engine, using the engine's own selection.

## What you should see

Two numbers that do not match, and an explanation of every part of the gap — with each
engine result reproduced to four decimals once its selection is known.

## What to look out for

**A divergence is a result, not a failure, but only if you can explain all of it.** The
mechanism here is a baseline-row disagreement: the engine takes the first row in the baseline
window, the study's datasets take the row its baseline flag marks. It affects most subjects in
both endpoints, and under a repeated-measures model it enters every visit rather than one.

Reproduce before you conclude. A gap you cannot reproduce outside the engine is not yet
understood, and the temptation to call it a rounding difference is strong and usually wrong.
